orchestrator.description: Coordinates multi-agent work, selects specialists and workflows, enforces handoffs, and verifies completion across Retro Messenger.

solution-architect.description: Use for architecture decisions, module boundaries, deployment topology, scalability, ADRs, and cross-cutting changes.

product-owner.description: Use to convert product requests into testable specifications, business rules, acceptance criteria, scope, and edge cases.

dotnet-backend.description: Use for ASP.NET Core, domain logic, application handlers, EF Core, Dapper, OpenIddict, Wolverine, Hangfire, and provider integrations.

realtime-signalr.description: Use for SignalR hubs, realtime contracts, connection lifecycle, groups, presence, typing, Buzz, receipts, and call signaling.

web-frontend.description: Use for the React web messenger, Fluent UI wrappers, IndexedDB, TanStack Query, Zustand, message timelines, and web accessibility.

electron-desktop.description: Use for Electron main/preload/renderer boundaries, windows, tray, native notifications, secure storage, SQLite, updates, and desktop Buzz.

react-native-mobile.description: Use for React Native mobile, SQLite, foreground/background lifecycle, push, SignalR, LiveKit, native permissions, and calls.

admin-portal.description: Use for the Refine and Ant Design admin portal, moderation, permissions, audit, feature flags, and operations dashboards.

database-postgresql.description: Use for PostgreSQL schema, migrations, indexes, query plans, concurrency, retention, backup, and data repair.

devops-observability.description: Use for Docker, CI/CD, Nginx, deployment, health checks, OpenTelemetry, monitoring, backup, releases, and rollback.

security-reviewer.description: Use proactively for authentication, authorization, uploads, Electron IPC, mobile storage, admin actions, privacy, and threat review.

qa-automation.description: Use for unit, integration, contract, E2E, load, concurrency, failure-mode, and regression test design or implementation.

code-reviewer.description: Use after implementation to review correctness, architecture, security, data integrity, concurrency, performance, tests, and documentation.
